boundaries.label: GLOBAL zone — template content only, no firm data
REGIONAL zone — one full deployment per region; firm data never leaves

cards.title: The 5 events we ask the existing systems to publish
items: The contract is the event. How each system emits it is its own implementation; we only require that no event is lost (we recommend an outbox, see the data-flow view)
Template Storage · TemplatePublished {template id, version, parent version, market, time}
Template Storage · TemplateWithdrawn {template id, version, time, reason}
Engagement Mgmt · EngagementCreated {engagement, firm, template id, version}
Engagement Mgmt · EngagementLoaded {engagement, firm, template id, current version}
Engagement Mgmt · UpdateDecided {engagement, version, apply/decline, summary id, user, time}
All are fat events in a CloudEvents envelope: metadata only, event id and per-emitter sequence
A market branch needs no extra event: it is a TemplatePublished whose parent is not the latest version

cards.title: What we change in the existing systems
items: Template Storage System: publishes 2 new events (TemplatePublished, TemplateWithdrawn)
Template Storage System: its events carry version, parent and market, and it provides a one-time listing of the lineage of versions already published
Engagement Mgmt System: publishes 3 new events (EngagementCreated, EngagementLoaded, UpdateDecided)
Recommended, so that no event is lost: an outbox table in the Product Template DB and in each customer database, with a relay per database that publishes rows until acknowledged
Engagement Mgmt System: its existing UI calls our Query API to show the pending indicator and the summary
Untouched: engagement storage format, the ~1 min load path, engagement creation flow

cards.title: Data ownership
items: Template versions and their lineage (parent, market, withdrawn): Template Storage (existing). How it stores lineage is its own decision
Generic summary of a version transition: Summary Service, stored in the Summaries DB (new, global, one instance)
Engagement and the effect of apply/decline: Engagement Mgmt (existing)
Current template version per engagement and the audit trail: Pending Updates DB (new, one per region)

Inside the Pending Updates DB the engagement events are the source of truth; the index, the copy of template versions and the copy of summaries are derived and can be rebuilt. Tables are in the data-model view

The two new databases are not connected to each other. When a TemplatePublished arrives, the Reconciler asks the Summary Service for one summary per version in use in its region (template and versions only, no firm data) and keeps a copy

cards.title: Event contract
items: This view shows the producer of each event. How an event physically travels (outbox → relay → broker → consumer → dead-letter queue) is in the data-flow view: event-delivery.html
Fat events, CloudEvents envelope, metadata only (never engagement content)
Event id + per-emitter sequence number
At-least-once delivery, idempotent consumer, dead-letter queue
Lost events: detected by published-vs-consumed counts and sequence gaps, repaired by replay from the outbox
Template events are broadcast: one publish, several subscribers (Summary Service and every region), each with its own queue
Engagement events have a single consumer, the Reconciler of their own region, and never leave it
The dead-letter queue is a setting of the Event Broker, so it is not a box here; it is drawn in the data-flow view

cards.title: Reconciler — three levels
items: 1. Outbox vs consumed: continuous, no loads, catches transport loss
2. On load: every user open compares the real version with the index (free; also does the backfill)
3. Background sweep: the worker forces loads for engagements nobody opens
A mismatch appends a 'Reconciled' event; nothing is overwritten

cards.title: Rollout and worker
items: Before the first firm: load the lineage of all versions already published into each region
Feature switched on firm by firm, only when all of a firm's engagements are indexed
Small firms first, several firms in parallel, quota per firm
All firms active in 30 days: 800,000 min / (30 × 1,440) ≈ 19 concurrent loads
Worker triggers: firm activation, a template publish (only for engagements not yet indexed) and the background sweep
'Pending' is computed as index × version cache, so 'within seconds' does not depend on the worker
On TemplatePublished the Reconciler writes the work to do in the Pending Updates DB; the worker takes it from there and records its progress (saga log) in the same database
When every engagement of a firm is indexed, the feature is switched on for that firm

cards.title: Assumptions
items: A loaded engagement exposes its current template version, not only the creation one
Engagement ids of a firm (with product) can be listed without loading them
An outbox table can be added to the Product Template DB and to the customer databases
Withdrawing a version is an action of Template Storage, so it can publish an event
The team that owns the pods sets our concurrency limit
Version Diff is used as given; Zip Handling is our assumption and is not touched
The Engagement Mgmt team can add the call to our Query API in its existing UI; the user never calls our API directly
Discarded alternative: a separate Version Catalog service (it would duplicate data that already has an owner). It is plan B if Template Storage cannot provide lineage in its events and as a listing
Template Storage knows parent version and market at publish time, and knows the lineage of versions already published. If it does not, the content teams must declare it once (risk)
We never read the Product Template DB directly: lineage reaches us through the events and the one-time listing
